_comment: Rolling-window estimates of the globalization coefficient on social security transfers, from 'Globalization and the Welfare State' (Nielsen, Chen & Jorgensen, 2026). Values are transcribed verbatim from Table 5.5 of the paper (verified against outputs/tables/gfc/rolling_snapshots.tex in the replication repo). The simulator offers whichever window lengths are present here.
_source: Table 5.5, p. 19. 10-year window, country-clustered standard errors.
_reproducibility_note: Do not regenerate this file without reading the note in scripts/generate-rolling-grid.py. As of commit 2218d27 of AntonEbsen/economics-of-the-welfare-state, running the repo's own rolling_ols_coefficients() on its own master_dataset.csv does NOT reproduce these published figures (e.g. overall/2023: paper 0.1831 (0.0679) vs code 0.1867 (0.0671); overall/2018: paper 0.1856 vs code 0.2776). The qualitative finding is unaffected — the coefficient still rises from roughly zero pre-2010 to strongly positive and significant post-2018 — but the exact numbers differ, so the published table is what ships here.
